land.text: the Transjuran duchy: 'the Central Plateau from the Jura Mountains up to the Great St Bernard Pass', with Geneva, Lausanne, Sion, Aargau, Bern and Valais, Franche-Comté and the estates around Besançon and Dole

predecessors.note: After Meerssen (870) Louis the German 'received most of the Upper Burgundy left to Lothair' (Treaty of Meerssen page); the Rudolf I page ties Rudolph's election to Charles the Fat's deposition (November 887).

land.text: the Kingdom of Burgundy of 933: Upper and Lower Burgundy united under Rudolph II

successors.note: Cliopatria's Kingdom of Arles (936, 117,221 km2) equals this state's 926 shape (45,842 km2) plus Lower Burgundy's (71,380 km2). The kingdom itself runs on to Rudolph II's death in 937 and Conrad.

capitals.name: Saint-Maurice d'Agaune
capitals.note: No opened page names a capital. Saint-Maurice is the abbey where the nobles and clergy elected Rudolph I in 888 and whose lay abbacy made him 'the most powerful magnate in Upper Burgundy' (Rudolf I page). Placeholder for a gap-filler; Rudolph II's seat is not given either.

rulers.name: Rudolph I
rulers.note: Elected king of Upper Burgundy at Saint-Maurice in 888; died 25 October 912 (the page gives that date); succeeded by his son Rudolph II.

rulers.name: Rudolph II
rulers.note: King of Italy 922-926 (crowned at Pavia, 924 on the Upper Burgundy page); rules the united Kingdom of Burgundy from 933; died 12 or 13 July 937, succeeded by Conrad the Peaceful. The dossier ends in 935 at the edge of Cliopatria's Kingdom of Arles.

correction.text: the shape unchanged; the kingdom exists from 888, not 887

keyframe_review.note: 887-895, 171 cells (41,536 km2); the page gives no area. The shape is right for the kingdom: 'the Central Plateau from the Jura Mountains up to the Great St Bernard Pass', Geneva, Lausanne, Sion, Aargau, Bern, Valais, Franche-Comté and the Besançon and Dole estates. Only the first year changes: Rudolph I was elected in 888, and 887 is still Charles the Fat's empire (he was deposed in November 887).
896-897, 171 cells: Rudolph I's kingdom unchanged. Arnulf 'acknowledged Rudolph's rule in Upper Burgundy' (Upper Burgundy page) after the Lotharingian war of 888-894.
898-898, 171 cells: Rudolph I's kingdom unchanged. Arnulf 'acknowledged Rudolph's rule in Upper Burgundy' (Upper Burgundy page) after the Lotharingian war of 888-894.
899-899, 171 cells: Rudolph I's kingdom unchanged. Arnulf 'acknowledged Rudolph's rule in Upper Burgundy' (Upper Burgundy page) after the Lotharingian war of 888-894.

900-910, 171 cells: Rudolph I's kingdom unchanged (one fewer cell at the Franche-Comté edge). Arnulf 'acknowledged Rudolph's rule in Upper Burgundy' (Upper Burgundy page) after the Lotharingian war of 888-894.

911-921, 173 cells: two cells near Besançon added (Franche-Comté, 5.7-8.1 E); the opened pages date nothing there, so the shape stands. Rudolph II succeeded in 912; his Swabian war (916-922) moved no border on the pages (Basel occupied 916, defeat at Winterthur 919, peace 922).

correction.text: the shape unchanged for 926-930; 931-932 and 933-935 follow as new keyframes

keyframe_review.note: 926-935, 189 cells (45,842 km2): 17 Swiss cells added (lon 7.4-8.5 E, lat 47.0-47.6 N: Basel, Aargau, Solothurn). Rudolph II 'gave the Holy Lance to Henry the Fowler in exchange for the Swabian Basel estates' in '926 or 935'. Valid as drawn for 926-930; from 931 the Viennois and Lyonnais are added and from 933 all of Lower Burgundy, so 931 and 933 become new keyframes. The kingdom is in Italy 923-926, which is not drawn here (ledger: contest).

correction.text: Upper Burgundy with the Viennois and Lyonnais

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 931-932: 'In 931, he [Hugh] bribed Rudolph off with the Viennois and Lyonnais, which Rudolph occupied.'

correction.text: the Kingdom of Burgundy: Upper Burgundy united with Lower Burgundy and Provence

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 933-935: 'the two Burgundian realms (Upper and Lower) were unified from 933, under Rudolph's rule' and the West Francia page: 'Rudolph II of Burgundy established the Kingdom of Burgundy in 933'. Cliopatria shows this union only from 936, as the Kingdom of Arles; the union of the two Cliopatria shapes (45,842 + 71,493 km2) is within 0.1% of the Arles area (117,221 km2).

correction.text: Upper Burgundy without the Italian kingdom (Rudolph II's Italian reign is the contest 923-926)

keyframe_review.note: 922-925, 828 cells (213,604 km2): Upper Burgundy (about 190 cells) plus about 616 Italian cells. Rudolph II 'was crowned king at Pavia' (the Upper Burgundy page says 924; the Rudolf II page gives his Italian reign as 922-926), defeated Berengar at Fiorenzuola on 17 July 923, and in 926 'Italian nobles turned against him'. Italy is the Kingdom of Italy's land, held by Berengar I until his murder in 924; it is drawn as a contest zone 923-926 (ledger), and the shape here is Upper Burgundy alone.

correction.text: empty: the Burgundian kingdom is the Kingdom of Arles from 936; this polygon is the duchy of Burgundy, in West Francia

keyframe_review.note: 936-946, 133 cells (31,793 km2), bbox 2.4-5.6 E, 46.1-48.3 N: the Burgundy of Auxerre, Autun and Dijon, not the kingdom. The Upper Burgundy page ends the kingdom in 933 (united with Lower Burgundy), and Cliopatria's Kingdom of Arles (936) already holds both Burgundies. This land is the West Frankish duchy of Burgundy: Richard the Justiciar was count of Autun from 880 and duke by 918, and the separate Burgundian realms of 879 and 888 'did not affect the north-western counties, which stayed in the West Frankish kingdom' (Duchy of Burgundy page). Cliopatria's Duchy of Burgundy row starts only in 1003. The West Franks dossier takes the land. Empty here.

Cliopatria's Duchy of Burgundy row starts only in 1003. The West Franks dossier takes the land. Empty here.

region.text: Geneva, Lausanne, Sion, Aargau, Bern, Valais, Franche-Comté, Besançon and Dole

ledger.note: 888: Rudolph I is elected king of Upper Burgundy at Saint-Maurice. 'The nobles and leading clergy of Upper Burgundy assembled at the Abbey of St. Maurice, Agaunum' and elected and crowned him, after Charles the Fat's deposition (Rudolf I page); the realm is 'the Central Plateau from the Jura Mountains up to the Great St Bernard Pass'.
888: Rudolph claims all of Lotharingia. 'Apparently on the basis of this election, Rudolph claimed the whole of Lotharingia', taking much of modern Lorraine and Alsace, until Arnulf forced him back.

894: the fighting with Arnulf ends. Arnulf 'rapidly forced Rudolph to abandon Lotharingia in return for recognition as king of Upper Burgundy'; hostilities 'seem to have continued intermittently until 894'.

region.text: the Besançon edge of the Franche-Comté

ledger.note: 911: Cliopatria's shape adds two cells near Besançon. The opened pages date nothing there (the Upper Burgundy page only names the Franche-Comté estates around Besançon and Dole); recorded as a bridge, not a fact.
916: Rudolph II occupies Basel. 'In 916 Rudolph II occupied Basel' in his border conflict with the Swabian dukes (Rudolf II page: he first campaigned in the Thurgau and Zürich estates).

region.text: Pavia and the Lombard plain where Berengar I was defeated

ledger.note: 923: Rudolph II fights for Italy. Invited in 922 by Margrave Adalbert I of Ivrea, he 'defeated Berengar at the Battle of Fiorenzuola' on 17 July 923 and was crowned king at Pavia (924 on the Upper Burgundy page). The page names Pavia and Fiorenzuola; the zone is the Lombard-Piedmont plain.

region.text: Pavia and the Lombard plain where Berengar I was defeated

ledger.note: 926: Rudolph loses Italy. 'Italian nobles turned against him and asked Hugh of Arles to rule instead'; Rudolph's father-in-law Burchard was killed near Novara and Rudolph returned to Upper Burgundy.

926: Basel passes to Rudolph. He 'gave the Holy Lance to Henry the Fowler in exchange for the Swabian Basel estates' in 926 or 935 (the page gives both); Cliopatria adds Basel and Aargau cells in 926.
926: the Basel estates and the Aargau edge are added to Upper Burgundy (17 Swiss cells in Cliopatria's 926 shape). The year is 926 or 935 on the page.
931: Rudolph II receives the Viennois and Lyonnais. 'In 931, he bribed Rudolph off with the Viennois and Lyonnais, which Rudolph occupied.'

region.text: Provence and the rest of Lower Burgundy

ledger.note: 933: Rudolph II takes Provence and unites the Burgundies. Hugh ceded 'his claims to Lower Burgundy in exchange for Rudolph's renunciation of Italian claims'; 'the two Burgundian realms (Upper and Lower) were unified from 933, under Rudolph's rule'.

933: Upper Burgundy becomes the Kingdom of Burgundy. 'Upper Burgundy was reunited with Lower Burgundy to form the Kingdom of Burgundy'; the West Francia page: 'Rudolph II of Burgundy established the Kingdom of Burgundy in 933'. Colour and dossier continue.
935: the dossier ends where Cliopatria's Upper Burgundy row ends (935) and its Kingdom of Arles begins (936). The kingdom itself goes on: Rudolph II died in 937 and Conrad the Peaceful succeeded him.

wars.name: Rudolph I's Lotharingian war with Arnulf
wars.outcome: Rudolph claims all Lotharingia in 888; Arnulf 'rapidly forced Rudolph to abandon Lotharingia in return for recognition as king of Upper Burgundy'; skirmishing continues intermittently to 894.

wars.name: Rudolph II and Burchard II of Swabia
wars.outcome: Rudolph occupies Basel (916), is defeated by Burchard II at the Battle of Winterthur (919) and makes peace in 922, marrying Burchard's daughter Bertha; the Basel estates come to him in 926 or 935.

wars.name: Rudolph II's Italian campaign

zones.text: Pavia and the Lombard plain where Berengar I was defeated

wars.outcome: Invited by Adalbert I of Ivrea, Rudolph defeats Berengar at Fiorenzuola (17 July 923) and is crowned at Pavia; Berengar is murdered in 924; in 926 the Italian nobles turn to Hugh of Arles and Rudolph returns to Upper Burgundy.
wars.note: The Upper Burgundy page dates the coronation 924, the Rudolf II page gives his reign as 922-926.

wars.name: Rudolph II and Hugh of Italy over Burgundy
wars.outcome: Hugh 'unsuccessfully attempted to take Burgundy from Rudolph's son, Rudolph II', buys him off with the Viennois and Lyonnais (931) and in 933 gives Provence for Rudolph's renunciation of Italy.

certainty.note: The realm is described by regions and estates, not by treaty lines; the Swabian frontier at Basel and the Italian conquest of 923-926 are approximate.

sources.title: Duchy of Burgundy
sources.note: The north-western counties stayed West Frankish; Richard the Justiciar; basis for marking the 936-959 shapes wrong.

notes: Merged rows: Cliopatria's 'Upper Burgundy' (887-959) and 'Upper Burgundy and Italy' (922-925) share Q33235 and the Wikipedia title 'Upper Burgundy'; the second is Rudolph II's Italian reign, so they are one state and are reviewed here under the earlier slug. upper-burgundy-and-italy gets no dossier of its own. Cliopatria's 'Upper Burgundy' 936-959 (133 cells) is not the Burgundian kingdom but the West Frankish duchy of Burgundy around Auxerre, Autun and Dijon (marked wrong); the Kingdom of Burgundy is the Kingdom of Arles from 936 (the Arles shape equals this state's 926 shape plus Lower Burgundy's). The West Franks dossier keeps the duchy as West Frankish land. A dossier for the duchy of Burgundy before 1003 (Richard the Justiciar 880/918; Cliopatria's Duchy of Burgundy starts in 1003) is needed. Italy: Cliopatria draws Rudolph II's Italian reign (922-926) as about 616 Italian cells inside this state and has no Kingdom of Italy shape for 922-935; the kingdom-of-italy dossier (eu-13) should cover those years, and here Italy is a contest zone only. Unsettled: no opened page names a capital (Saint-Maurice d'Agaune is a placeholder), gives the month of the 888 election, or settles whether the Basel exchange was in 926 or 935. The dossier ends in 935, two years before Rudolph II's death, to meet the Kingdom of Arles; the Swabian counterpart is written as a name because no Duchy of Swabia row exists in polities.csv. Infobox of the Upper Burgundy page gives no area.
